featured_videos.title: 7 Carnivore Mistakes That Are Keeping You Fat
featured_videos.creator: Richard Smith
featured_videos.editorial_title: 7 Carnivore Mistakes That Are Keeping You Fat
featured_videos.commentary: The comments here are really telling. People are waking up to the fact that "fat is good" doesn't mean "unlimited fat is good," and that's the exact reality check our audience needs. One commenter nailed it: they've been using butter and cream as a guilt-free pass, but it's actually working against their weight loss goals. That's not a carnivore failure, that's just physics catching up. What's interesting is how many people are realizing they need to dial back the add-ons (the coffee butter, the snacking) while keeping the meat solid, and suddenly the stubborn last 10 pounds start moving. This is way more nuanced than "eat more fat to lose fat," and it feels like the community is finally getting comfortable saying that out loud.

featured_videos.title: Your Carnivore Diet Doesn't Have To Look Like Mine
featured_videos.creator: Meet Carnivore
featured_videos.editorial_title: Your Carnivore Diet Doesn't Have To Look Like Mine
featured_videos.commentary: This is exactly what I tell people in coaching calls. You can follow someone else's carnivore to the letter and feel worse than they do, because you're not them. Your gut bacteria aren't the same, your stress levels aren't the same, your food sensitivities aren't the same. The community here nailed it, too, especially whoever said carnivore is a starting point, not a goal. Some of you thrive on strict muscle meat. Others do better with cheese, pickles, coffee, even the occasional grilled cheese. What matters most is that you feel good and you can actually stick with it long-term, not that you're following someone's Instagram version perfectly. The "carnivore police" comment made me laugh because it's real, but here's the truth: if you've lost 120 pounds eating cheese and coffee on carnivore, you've already proven it works for you. Stop apologizing for it.

featured_videos.title: 6 Micro Carnivore Habits That Will ACTUALLY Drop Inches Fast (140lbs Lost)
featured_videos.creator: Carnivore Claire
featured_videos.editorial_title: 6 Micro Carnivore Habits That Will ACTUALLY Drop Inches Fast (140lbs Lost)
featured_videos.commentary: Claire's hitting on something the community keeps circling back to. these aren't sexy fixes, they're just accountability. What's wild is how many people in the comments mention breaking out of a stall the second they started paying attention again. One viewer went from dabbling in and out for a year to committing after stepping on the scale and facing reality. That's the thing about micro habits. They're boring. They work anyway. The "weigh daily" debate especially resonates because it flips the script. instead of white-knuckling willpower, you're just staying honest with yourself. No magic supplement, no special protocol, just showing up.

featured_videos.title: My Doctor’s Warning: Why he turned against my carnivore diet.
featured_videos.creator: The Carnivore Fix
featured_videos.editorial_title: My Doctor’s Warning: Why he turned against my carnivore diet.
featured_videos.commentary: What strikes me most about this comment section isn't the frustration with doctors, it's that so many people are choosing silence over conversation. They're not lying to their doctors, exactly, just editing what they share. And I get it. I've coached women who've done the same thing, especially when they've already felt dismissed about their health choices. But here's what I've learned: the real problem isn't your doctor's opinion about carnivore, it's that most doctors have never seen real metabolic healing happen this way. They weren't trained in it. The system didn't teach them. That doesn't make them puppets, it makes them limited. The good news? There ARE practitioners who understand this now, and if your current doctor is warning you away while you're getting healthier. losing weight, ditching medications, feeling better. that's worth a serious conversation about whether you're on the same team anymore.

featured_videos.title: What I Eat: Food Delivery on a Carnivore Diet
featured_videos.creator: Laura Spath
featured_videos.editorial_title: What I Eat: Food Delivery on a Carnivore Diet
featured_videos.commentary: Laura nailed something the travel crowd desperately needs to hear: you don't have to choose between eating carnivore and living a normal life on the road. The comments are full of pilots, traveling professionals, and people who thought the diet meant either packing coolers or eating salads at airport restaurants, and watching her problem-solve with delivery apps and restaurant hacks is clearly shifting that narrative. What stuck with me is how many commenters are sharing their own workarounds, snow crab legs and frozen burger packs in suitcases, because once you see it's possible, you start thinking like an engineer instead of giving up. The real win here is that she's showing people it's not about willpower or restrictions when you travel, it's about having a protocol before you leave home, and that's exactly the mindset that makes carnivore stick long-term instead of becoming another diet you quit on business trips.

featured_videos.title: I REFUSED Doctor's Orders Because of YOU! October Challenge
featured_videos.creator: Carnivore Quest
featured_videos.editorial_title: I REFUSED Doctor's Orders Because of YOU! October Challenge
featured_videos.commentary: Watching the comments roll in, I'm struck by how many people are sharing specific wins that doctors said weren't possible. One person went from high 80s oxygen levels to consistently 93-95. Another ditched blood pressure meds after adding potassium and electrolytes. These aren't anecdotes, they're patterns, and they matter because they show what happens when someone actually commits instead of just listening to blanket medical advice. The walking challenge resonates because it's real and sustainable, not some extreme hack. That's what I see work in coaching too, people just need permission to trust what their own body is telling them.
